blocks.name: Digital & analogue signals
blocks.definition: Know the difference between a digital and analogue signal

blocks.md:
- There are two types of signals:

  - analogue
  - digital
- **Analogue signals vary continuously** - they can take any value

blocks.alt: Graph of signal strength versus time showing a green sinusoidal wave with two peaks and two troughs.
blocks.caption: An analogue signal is continuously varying, taking any value

blocks.md:
- **A digital signal can only take one of two (discrete) states**

  - These are usually referred to as:
  
    - **1**s and **0**s
    - **high**s and **low**s
    - **on**s and **off**s

blocks.alt: Graph of digital signal strength against time, showing a square wave switching between 0 and 1 with two high pulses separated by a low interval.
blocks.caption: A digital signal can only take one of two values – 0 or 1

blocks.name: Transmission of sound
blocks.definition: Know that a sound can be transmitted as a digital or analogue signal

blocks.md: - Sound waves can be transmitted as a **digital** or **analogue** signal

- Signals for speech or music are made up of varying frequencies

  - To make out the information clearly, the signal needs to be transmitted with as little interference as possible

- The signal undergoes **digital sampling**
- It is converted **both before transmission** and **after being received**

  - Before transmission: the signal is converted from **analogue** to **digital**
  - After being received: the signal is converted back from **digital** to **analogue**

blocks.alt: Diagram comparing a smooth green analogue sine wave with a blue stepped digital signal approximating it, each labelled with arrows.
blocks.caption: Digitally sampling an analogue signal

blocks.md:
- The key **advantages** of data transmission in **digital** form compared to analogue are:

  - The signal can be ***regenerated*** so there is minimal ***noise***
  - Due to accurate signal regeneration, the **range** of digital signals is **larger** than the range of analogue signals (they can **cover larger distances**)
  - Digital signals enable an **increased rate of data transmission **compared to analogue
  - Extra data can be added so that the signal can be checked for errors

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md: Remember that digital sampling is when you convert an analogue signal into a digital signal by recording sound at set time intervals.
